clue.text: Moved hods wearing sensible footwear (8)

indicators.note: the letters of HODS are moved about
SANE wears the new letters, holding them inside

explanation.surface: A builder's labourer carries hods about in practical shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible footwear' reads as one phrase, but 'sensible' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandshoe is a plimsoll, a light canvas shoe with a rubber sole: an example of footwear.

clue.text: Hot German Christmas cake one left out (6)

indicators.note: one L, for left, is literally left out of the cake's name

blocks.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas
L = left; drop one of the cake's two L's

explanation.surface: A German Christmas cake served hot, with one slice left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' seems to describe the cake straight from the oven; here it is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: 'hot' goods are ones recently taken by theft and still risky to sell.

clue.text: Line penned by Victorian author? I don’t think so! (6)

indicators.note: the L is enclosed, as if in a pen, by the author's name

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a certain line was written by a Victorian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' pretends to be about authorship, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'Hardly!' on its own is a sceptical retort, as dismissive as 'I don't think so!'

clue.text: Academic’s third paper up for discussion (2,5)

indicators.note: take the third letter of 'Academic'

explanation.surface: A scholar's third paper is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic's third paper' looks like a numbered publication; the third is only a letter of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the point at issue is the one being argued over right now.

clue.text: Boat rather packed with deckchairs in the middle (8)

indicators.note: SOONER is packed with the other letters
take the two central letters of 'deckchairs'

blocks.note: the middle two letters of the ten in deCKCHairs, placed inside S…OONER

explanation.surface: A boat crammed with deckchairs in the middle of the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Deckchairs fit the nautical picture neatly, which hides that only their two central letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner, a sailing vessel with two or more masts, is one kind of boat.

clue.text: Misleading promise of payment included in project details (8)

indicators.note: to be included in something is to sit within it, so IOU goes inside SPECS

blocks.note: specs = specifications, the details of a project
an IOU ('I owe you') is a written promise to pay, placed inside SPEC…S

explanation.surface: A deceptive promise to pay has been buried in a project's paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promise of payment' could be any pledge; the crossword's usual one is the three-letter IOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a specious claim looks sound on the surface but is false, so it misleads.

clue.text: Soap maybe picked up; it’s usually sold in boxes (6)

indicators.note: picked up as in heard: the word sounds like another

blocks.note: a soap opera is an example of a serial

explanation.surface: A bar of soap is picked up from the shop shelf, sold boxed like washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests something to wash with, and boxes suggest soap powder; it is really a TV soap opera, a kind of serial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description rather than a synonym: breakfast cereal comes in cardboard boxes.

clue.text: Dodgy plastic pipes around museum pieces cracked and leaked, perhaps (4,11)

indicators.note: dodgy pipes are unsound, so their letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go around ART

blocks.note: PLASTIC PIPES rearranged, split to go around the next piece
the art in a museum, sitting inside PASTP…ICIPLES

explanation.surface: Dodgy plastic plumbing around museum exhibits has cracked and leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked and leaked' reads as what the pipes did, but the definition is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'cracked' and 'leaked' are both past participles of verbs, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: After a couple of days, was the person in charge confused? (6)

blocks.note: A + DD, two D's for days

explanation.surface: After two days in charge, a manager wonders whether they have lost the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts LED after ADD. D = day is a standard abbreviation, so a couple of days is DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an addled mind, like a rotten egg, is muddled and unable to think straight.

clue.text: Frustrated senior journo pursuing hard liquor (8)

indicators.note: to pursue is to chase from behind, so ED comes after SCOTCH

explanation.surface: A frustrated editor chases after a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frustrated' seems to describe the journalist's mood, but it defines the answer in its sense of thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scotch a plan or rumour is to put a stop to it, thwarting it.

clue.text: You shouldn’t have stood up periodically hiding something up your sleeve? (5,3)

indicators.note: take every other letter of 'stood up'
TOU hides HANKY inside it

blocks.note: the even letters of sToOd Up
a handkerchief tucked up a sleeve, placed inside T…OU

explanation.surface: Someone stood up in a funny way, as if concealing a trick up their sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something up your sleeve' suggests a secret plan, but here it is literal: people keep hankies there.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'You shouldn't have!' is what one says on receiving a gift, a polite way to express gratitude.

clue.text: Bit of ramen ultimately eaten a lot, but not quite finished (6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'eaten'
the last letter of OODLES is missing

blocks.clueFragment: a lot, but not quite finished
blocks.note: OODLES = a lot, with its final S dropped

explanation.surface: A diner has eaten a lot of ramen but not quite finished the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a meal left unfinished; 'not quite finished' actually trims a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Part for whole: ramen is a Japanese soup made of wheat noodles, so one strand is a bit of it.

clue.text: Carry on being cheeky about female relative (7)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around, so PERT surrounds SIS

explanation.surface: Someone keeps being cheeky about their sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on being cheeky' reads as a single scolding, but the definition stops at 'Carry on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean continue steadily despite obstacles.

clue.text: Posts secured at the front with one stud, possibly (5,3)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'secured'
ONE STUD could possibly be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fence posts are secured at the front with a single stud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' looks like wooden stakes, which is what 'secured' and 'stud' support; it is the verb for mailing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym of the verb: to post letters is to dispatch them by mail.

clue.text: I need help taking on case for philosopher (8)

indicators.note: SOS takes CRATE on board, inside it

blocks.note: a crate is a packing case, placed inside SO…S

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help taking on a legal case for a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a trial, and the Athenian thinker famously had one, but it means a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the classical Greek thinker who taught Plato.

clue.text: Love one playing Disintegration (7)

blocks.note: on = playing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A loved one is playing Disintegration, the album by The Cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Disintegration look like a record title (it is The Cure's 1989 album), but it is also the plain word the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: wind and water wear rock away bit by bit until it crumbles apart.

clue.text: Upset created by obvious item you can dispense with? (8)

explanation.surface: Someone is upset because a pointless item is being thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispense with' usually means do without; read literally, an urn is something you dispense drinks with.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the physical sense: to upset a canoe or a vase is to tip it over.

clue.text: Admirer cheers to support popular Spanish princess (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, FAN TA sits beneath IN, holding it up

explanation.surface: An admirer toasts a well-loved Spanish princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' reads as a toast but here means thanks, as it often does in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: the Spanish word for a daughter of the king, used in English for such royals.

clue.text: Widely recognised architectural style outside capital of Crete (6)

indicators.note: the style stands outside, on either side of, the letter, so it wraps around it
the capital, or first, letter of Crete

blocks.note: the Ionic order of classical columns
first letter of Crete, placed inside I…ONIC

explanation.surface: A famous building style stands just outside Heraklion, capital of Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Crete' sends the mind to Heraklion; it is only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a landmark or image known by almost everyone and treated as a symbol.

clue.text: Dish taken from church illicitly (6)

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plate has been stolen from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' pretends to be a piece of church plate, stolen; it is a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for chilli con carne, a spicy stew of minced beef and beans served as a meal.

clue.text: Elegant features of associations in a French resort? (8)

explanation.surface: A travel writer admires the elegant features of connections found in a French resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: associations in Nice are 'Nice ties'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fine points of manners or detail, the refinements that make something polished.

clue.text: Extremely cocky tennis champ is somewhat mechanical individual (6)

indicators.note: take the extreme, outer letters of 'cocky'

blocks.note: the first and last letters of CockY

explanation.surface: A very cocky tennis champion plays like a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Borg was famous for ice-cool, almost robotic play, so the surface fits. 'Somewhat' is fair because the answer is only partly machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Science-fiction term for a being that is part human, part machine.

clue.text: Cut, in a way, assistance for driver, mostly at that time (6)

indicators.note: most of THEN, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: a golf tee holds the ball up for a drive
THEN = at that time, minus the N

explanation.surface: A motorist gets help, cut short and mostly at that particular moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist but is a golfer's club.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: babies are said to cut their teeth, so 'cut, in a way' describes a baby getting them.

clue.text: Family experiences in South America and somewhere in Africa (8)

indicators.note: 'in' read literally as placed inside, so HAS goes within SA

blocks.note: has = experiences (has fun), placed inside S…A

explanation.surface: A family's travels take in South America and somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long itinerary, so it is easy to miss that South America is only two letters wrapped round a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately vague: the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, one place among many in Africa.

clue.text: Animal noises filling stable at sunset (6)

indicators.note: the answer fills the middle of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Sheep and goats call out as they fill the stable at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' invites an anagram of its letters, which gives the right letters but leaves 'filling' and 'at sunset' unused. The answer runs across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The calls of sheep and goats, a specific kind of animal sound.

clue.text: Part of the UK rioters trashed with such glee (15)

indicators.note: the letters are trashed, thrown into disorder

explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately vague: one county in western England, so one region of the United Kingdom.
